legal.prevails: The Traditional Chinese text is the authoritative version. The English text is a translation; where the two differ, the Chinese text prevails.
privacy.changes: If this policy changes, we post the new version on this page with a new date. If a change affects your rights, or how we collect, process or use your data, including what we collect and who receives it, we also write to the address you sign in with at least {$days} days before it takes effect.
privacy.cookies: When you sign in, the service sets one cookie, {$cookie}. It keeps you signed in for {$days} days or until you sign out, and only this site can read it. The service sets no other cookie and uses no analytics, advertising or tracking tools. The other sites a digest page contacts are listed under “Who else receives it”.
privacy.deletion: When you write to ask us to delete your data, we finish within {$days} days of your request: we take your address off the invite list, which ends your sessions and deletes your sign-in records, and we delete the data in your digest's database by hand. After that, these remain: the daily backups, until they expire (see “How long we keep it”); Cloudflare's logs, until their own period ends; what Anthropic received to write the summaries, which Anthropic's own terms govern; the alerts of failed runs in the operator's Discord channel; and the run records, AI spend and schedule the registry holds under your digest's id, which we keep as the service's operating record and which do not hold your email address. A copy we send you is an export of your digest's database, in the format the daily backup uses.
privacy.description: What the Cyris hosted beta keeps about its readers, where it is kept, and who else receives it.
privacy.intro: Cyris makes a digest of the feeds and newsletters its readers choose. This hosted service is a free, invite-only closed beta, run by an individual under the name Cyris (“we”). This policy says what the service keeps about you, where it is kept, who else receives it, and how to ask us about it. We handle your personal data under the Personal Data Protection Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan).
privacy.kept_account: Your email address, the digest it may sign in to, and when you were invited.
privacy.kept_digest: Your digest: its sources (feed addresses and newsletter senders), its settings, the articles fetched from those sources with their text, the issues made from them and their pages, and the votes you cast on its articles. Each digest has one reader.
privacy.kept_logs: Logs: Cloudflare keeps a log of each request to the service and of each run's output (Workers Logs). It can include connection details such as the time and address of a request and your IP address. Cloudflare keeps these logs for up to {$days} days. The lines the service writes itself name your digest by its id, and are designed to hold neither your email address nor a sign-in token.
privacy.kept_newsletters: Newsletter mail sent to your digest's own random address: its sender, subject, date, body and some of its headers. A newsletter can hold anything its sender put in it, such as your name. Your digest's next run turns each message one of its sources matches into an article and deletes the message; a message no source matches is deleted after {$days} days.
privacy.kept_sign_in: Your sign-ins: each sign-in link and each session, stored as a hash of its token, not the token itself, with your email address and when it expires. A link expires after {$minutes} minutes and a session after {$days} days. Each link you ask for on the sign-in page is also recorded with your address and the time; once that record is a day old, it is cleared the next time anyone asks for a sign-in link.
privacy.kept_spend: What your digest's AI use cost: for each run, the model, the tokens it used and their cost, and for each month, the total. And a record of each run: when it was queued, started and ended, and how it ended.
privacy.operator: The operator's tools can read and change any digest's data. We use them on your digest only to answer a support request, to look into an incident or a failed run, to deal with abuse, or when the law requires it. Those tools do not yet keep a record of each time they are used. The operator also sees a routine report of every digest: its sources, its runs, its AI spend, and the sender and subject of each newsletter waiting in it, but not their bodies.
privacy.operator_heading: When we look at your data
privacy.recipient_anthropic: Anthropic writes the summaries. Each run sends the text of the articles and newsletters in your digest, with your digest's instructions such as its style and output language, to Anthropic's API, to the model {$model}.
privacy.recipient_browser: A digest page loads its fonts from Google Fonts and each article's picture from the site that published it, so your browser contacts those sites when you open the page. The sign-in pages, this page and the settings page load nothing from any other site.
privacy.recipient_cloudflare: Cloudflare hosts the service and stores the data above. It also sends the sign-in mail, and receives the newsletter mail sent to your digest's address.
privacy.recipient_discord: When a run fails, an alert naming your digest's id and the error goes to the operator's channel on Discord.
privacy.required: You are free to decide whether to give us your data. Your email address is needed to sign in, so without it you cannot use the service. Sources and settings are yours to choose; with no sources, no digest is made.
privacy.retention: Your digest's data is kept while you use the service. We delete it within {$deletion} days after you ask us to (see “Your rights”) or after we end your access. We also delete it once you have gone {$months} months without signing in: {$reminder} days before that, we write to the address you sign in with to remind you, and signing in once starts the count again. The service does not yet record the date you last signed in; once it does, the {$months} months run from that day or from your latest sign-in after it, and we will tell you when it starts, in the way this policy's changes are announced. If the beta is to end, we tell you at least {$end} days before, as the terms say. Every day the service exports each digest's database, and the registry, to Cloudflare R2 storage as a backup. Each export is set to expire {$days} days after it is uploaded, and Cloudflare usually removes it within {$hours} hours of that. So data we have deleted can stay in the backups for up to about {$most} days.
privacy.rights: Under the Personal Data Protection Act you may ask to see your data or have a copy of it, to have it completed or corrected, to have us stop collecting, processing or using it, or to have it deleted. There is no page for this yet: write to {$privacy} from the address you sign in with. We answer a request to see your data or have a copy of it within {$see} days, and a request to complete, correct or stop within {$change} days. If we need longer, we will write to tell you why, and the extension is at most {$see} and {$change} more days. A request to delete is done within {$deletion} days, as below.
privacy.safeguards: We take reasonable steps to protect your data: the service's links use encrypted (HTTPS) connections and the sign-in cookie travels only over them, sign-in tokens are kept only as hashes, each digest has its own database, and the operator's tools need a separate credential. No system can be guaranteed secure. When we learn that your personal data has been stolen, altered, damaged, lost or leaked, we will tell you, as the law requires, by writing to the address you sign in with.
privacy.security: To report a security problem, write to {$security}.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.use: We use your data to sign you in, to fetch your sources and make your digest, to keep the service running and within its costs, and to answer you. We do not sell it and we show you no advertising. We give it to no one other than the companies named below, unless the law requires us to.
privacy.where: The data above is kept on Cloudflare. Your digest's data is in a database of its own, kept apart from other digests by design; the sign-in records, the invite list and the AI spend are in one registry the service keeps for every digest. We tell Cloudflare that we prefer western North America for both, and Cloudflare decides where they actually are. The companies named below also process what they receive outside Taiwan. So your data is transferred, stored and processed outside Taiwan, mainly in the United States.
terms.age: The service is for people aged 18 or over.
terms.availability: We provide the service as it is. We do not guarantee that it is always available, that a digest is made on time, or that a digest is complete or free of errors. Summaries are written by an AI model and can be wrong: check the original article before you rely on one.
terms.beta: The service is a closed beta: only an address we have invited can sign in. It is free. We pay for the AI that writes your digest, so each digest has a monthly AI allowance; once a month's allowance is spent, the digest's runs that month go on without AI.
terms.changes: We may change these terms; the date above says when they last changed. If a change affects your rights or obligations, we write to the address you sign in with at least {$days} days before it takes effect. If you do not agree, you can stop using the service and ask us to delete your data; if you keep using it after the change takes effect, you accept the new terms.
terms.content: The articles and newsletters in your digest belong to their publishers. The service fetches them only to make your digest, which is for you to read, not to republish.
terms.description: The terms of the Cyris hosted beta.
terms.end: We may change the beta at any time, and we may end your access to it at any time. When we do, we write to tell you, and until your data is deleted you can still ask for a copy of it. We end the beta itself only after writing to the address you sign in with at least {$days} days before; until it ends, you can ask for a copy of your data, as the privacy policy says. Only an urgent case, such as a security incident or a requirement of the law, may make us suspend or end the beta at once, and we then write to you afterwards.
terms.forum: If a dispute arises from these terms or the service, write to {$support} first and we will try to settle it with you. If it goes to court, the court is the one the laws of the Republic of China (Taiwan) name.
terms.intro: These terms govern your use of the Cyris hosted service, run by an individual under the name Cyris (“we”). By signing in, you accept them.
terms.law: These terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of China (Taiwan).
terms.leave: You can stop using the service at any time. To have us remove your access and delete your data, write to {$privacy}.
terms.liability: The service is a free beta. To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for loss that comes from using the service or from being unable to use it, including a digest that is late, incomplete or wrong. This does not apply to loss caused by our intent or gross negligence, or to any liability that the Consumer Protection Act, the Personal Data Protection Act or other law does not allow to be excluded or limited in advance.
terms.severability: If any part of these terms is invalid under the law, the rest stays in effect.
terms.title: Terms of service
terms.use: Use the service for your own reading. Do not try to reach another digest, the operator's tools or anyone else's account; do not overload the service or use it to break the law; and add only sources you may lawfully read.
vote.access_not_set_up: Access is not set up for this deployment. Ask the operator to finish the Cloudflare Access setup, then reload the page.
vote.not_configured: Voting is not set up here: the app Worker has no CYRIS_PROMOTE_WORKER_URL. Set it, then vote again.
vote.refused: The vote did not go through (HTTP {$status}). Try again; if it keeps failing, check the promote Worker.
vote.signed_out: Your session has ended, so the vote was not taken. Reload the page and sign in again.
vote.unanswered: No answer from the server, so the vote may not have been taken. Check your connection, then try again.
